dimensions.assessment: Affects bankruptcy trustees in Chapter 7 and Chapter 11 cases, court administrators, and specific federal districts with temporary judgeships.
dimensions.evidence: Trustees serving in bankruptcy cases under chapter 7 of title 11, United States Code, are vital to the functioning of the bankruptcy system

dimensions.assessment: Doubles the baseline case compensation for Chapter 7 trustees from $60 to $120 per case and extends judgeship terms and fee rules, presenting meaningful administrative and financial adjustments for those in the bankruptcy system.
dimensions.evidence: increasing the total compensation of trustees to $120 per case

dimensions.assessment: Involves specific statutory fee distributions and directs $5,400,000 of certain collected fees to the general fund of the Treasury annually for fiscal years 2026 through 2031.
dimensions.evidence: $5,400,000 of the fees collected under section 1930(a)(6) of title 28, United States Code, shall be deposited in the general fund of the Treasury

dimensions.assessment: Amends titles 11 and 28 of the United States Code regarding trustee compensation, fee destinations, and terms of temporary bankruptcy judgeships.
dimensions.evidence: To amend titles 11 and 28, United States Code, to modify the compensation payable to trustees serving in cases under chapter 7

dimensions.assessment: Extends various administrative fee authorities and temporary judgeships for an additional five to ten years, creating medium-to-long-term structural changes.
dimensions.evidence: the greater of 0.4 or and (II), in subclause (II), by striking 0.8 and inserting 0.9

missing_information: Exact total number of bankruptcy cases filed annually nationwide that will receive the new trustee compensation rate.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill adjusts bankruptcy trustee compensation, extends certain temporary judgeships and quarterly filing fee structures for five to ten years, and reallocates specific fee distributions across federal funds.

card.label: S. 1659
card.summary: The Bankruptcy Administration Improvement Act of 2025 makes adjustments to how the federal bankruptcy system is funded and administered. It increases the compensation paid to Chapter 7 bankruptcy trustees, extends and adjusts certain Chapter 11 quarterly bankruptcy fees, and extends the terms of specified temporary bankruptcy judgeships across various districts.
card.title: Bankruptcy Administration Improvement Act of 2025
